t: Section 901(a) of the Public Health Service Act is further amended by inserting at the end thereof the following new sentence: “For any fiscal year ending after June 30, 1969, such portion of the appropriations pursuant to this section as the Secretary may determine, but not exceeding 1 per centum thereof, shall be available to the Secretary for evaluation (directly or by grants or contracts) of the program authorized by this title.”

fable.w: This provision only sets aside up to 1 percent of appropriations for the Secretary to evaluate the program. The tempting reading is that "grants or contracts" bring outside parties in, but grantees and contractors performing evaluation work are not being consulted before a federal decision, and grants and contracts are expressly excluded. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall be available to the Secretary for evaluation (directly or by grants or contracts) of the program authorized by this title

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to use funds for program evaluation, either directly or through grants and contracts. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards involving non-federal members. The mention of 'grants or contracts' refers to the mechanism of funding the evaluation, not to a participatory decision-making process involving the public or outside entities in the government's decision.
qwen_block.s: such portion of the appropriations pursuant to this section as the Secretary may determine, but not exceeding 1 per centum thereof, shall be available to the Secretary for evaluation (directly or by grants or contracts) of the program authorized by this title.

opus.w: This provision only allows up to 1 percent of appropriations to be used for evaluating the program. It requires no public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities or right to sue. Outside grantees or contractors might do the evaluation work, but grants and contracts are explicitly excluded from participation, and they don't involve outsiders in any federal decision.
opus.s: shall be available to the Secretary for evaluation (directly or by grants or contracts) of the program authorized by this title
opus.b: The tempting reading is that evaluation "by grants or contracts" brings outside parties into the program. It fails because the definition excludes grants and contracts, and this provision only sets aside money. It requires no consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to object.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to use funds for program evaluation, either directly or through grants and contracts. The definition explicitly states that applications for grants or contracts are not participation. Additionally, the evaluation is an internal administrative action or a procurement of services, not a process of consulting with outside parties (such as the public, states, or advisory boards) before making a decision. The outside entities involved are contractors or grantees performing tasks, not participants in a decision-making forum.
qwen_chat.s: such portion of the appropriations pursuant to this section as the Secretary may determine, but not exceeding 1 per centum thereof, shall be available to the Secretary for evaluation (directly or by grants or contracts) of the program authorized by this title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "evaluation... by grants or contracts" involves outside parties (grantees/contractors) and thus constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses." Furthermore, the evaluation is conducted *by* the Secretary (or via hired contractors acting as agents), not *with* outside parties in a consultative or advisory capacity regarding a decision. The outside parties are service providers, not participants in the decision-making process.
